title: Proactive admission mediator with offline policy-sim and traffic-slicing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a proactive admission mediator for Dedicated fleets that combines lightweight online admission decisions with an offline policy-simulation service and traffic-slicing primitives. The mediator should improve P99 SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving throughput guarantees for batch/low-priority workloads.

Problem context: We currently rely on reactive admission (burst caps + token buckets) that reacts to overload after queues grow. This leads to tail latency spikes for latency-sensitive customers when sudden demand mixes with background heavy workloads. We need a system that can: (1) make early, cost-aware soft-deny decisions before queues saturate, (2) support traffic slicing (latency-sensitive vs best-effort lanes) with dynamic quota rebalancing, and (3) provide a policy-simulation environment to safely evaluate rollout impact on historical traces and synthetic bursts.

Scope: Design and implement mediator core (fast path), admission policy DSL (rules for tenant classes, cost budgets, deadlines), traffic-slice controller (rebalancing + reserved mini-pools), and an offline policy-sim service that runs policies against windowed traces to produce expected SLO/throughput/cost deltas. Integrations: Dedicated routing layer, autoscaler hint API, console dashboards (policy-sim results + rollout canary metrics).

Acceptance criteria:
- Mediator enforces soft-deny decisions within 1ms median decision latency under load.
- Policy-sim produces a per-tenant SLO/throughput delta estimate with >85% correlation to canary runs (on historical traces).
- Traffic-slicing supports at least two slices with configurable guaranteed min-throughput and burst headroom.
- Autoscaler receives usage hints from mediator to avoid oscillations during soft-deny transitions.
- End-to-end canary rollout documented and executed on a small fleet with monitoring dashboards and rollback triggers.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: Adding offline sim increases maintenance. Mitigation: make sim a standalone service with clear ingestion schemas and automated daily replay.
- Over-optimization: Aggressive soft-deny may hurt throughput; we default to conservative thresholds and require policy-sim approval before any production rollout.
- Observability: Need per-request tagging to reconcile sim vs production; will add lightweight tracing hooks in the runtime.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket to tackle mixed-workload tail latency. Initial design doc in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RINF/Proactive+Admission+Mediator

2026-02-25 - Marco Liu: Spike completed — baseline local simulator and simple token-reserve prototype. Findings: naive token reservation starves green traffic under high churn; need dynamic reclaiming and decay windows.

2026-03-01 - Design review (Elena Gomez): Suggested adding a deadline-aware scoring function and exposing per-tenant soft-deny reasons to Console. Also asked to limit policy DSL surface to simple predicates for initial launch.
2026-03-04 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/mediator/pull/412 — core fast-path admission plus slice config. Requesting review from runtime and autoscaler owners.

2026-03-07 - Marco Liu: Implemented traffic-slicing controller and autoscaler hint emitter. Local load tests: P99 for latency slice reduced by ~28% at 60% cluster saturation; batch throughput impact ~6%.
2026-03-09 - Product (Samir Rao) feedback: Request to add ‘customer_impact’ tagging to each policy for reporting and to allow quick policy overrides from Console.
2026-03-10 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed data flows; recommended KMS for policy store and ACLs for policy-sim trace access. Marked security_review_required=true for rollout gate.
